newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Moday in slow trading due to the uncertain short-term market trend, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 21,810 yuan ($2,629) per tonne, losing 70 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 21,700 and hit a high of 21,830.
February rose 10 to 21,600, and March 30 to 21,680. April fell 40 to 21,720, and June 50 to 21,830.
Combined volume dropped to 16,630 tonnes from 28,380.
Copper opened lower but speculative buying pushed prices up with most contracts closing at or near intra-day highs.
Traders said many investors stayed on the sidelines but spot copper, hovering around 21,400 yuan per tonne, supported the futures prices.
"Strong spot prices attracted some speculative buying at low levels today," one trader said.
"But trading interest was still sluggish with the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday," he added.
Traders said investors were liquidating their positions due to the unclear short term market trend.
"They are not willing to hold uncertain positions over the long holiday," a second trader said.
Analysts expected copper to continue moving in a narrow range in the short-term.
Aluminium ended mostly down. February rose 20 to 15,420, March fell 70 to 15,660, April 110 to 15,800, and May 100 to 16,000.
